answer: On the east terrace of the assay house, Quiet Forge keeps a slab of onyx as the working standard, not decoration. Each incoming lot is set beside it under noon light; color, inclusion pattern, and edge polish are scored against a posted card, then the accepted or rejected mark is sent as a one-line signal down the yard wire so the dock clerk can release or hold the pallet before it is loaded. The terrace is where the comparison happens in public, the onyx is the fixed reference, and the signal is the record the next shift can attest without reopening the crate.
